controls.label: x coordinate of observation 1
controls.help: Sets the x coordinate of observation 1. Changing the value changes predicted y for observation 1, residual 1, squared residual 1, the squared-residual vector, and total squared error.

controls.label: observed y of observation 1
controls.help: Sets the observed y coordinate of observation 1. Changing the value changes residual 1, squared residual 1, the squared-residual vector, and total squared error.

controls.label: x coordinate of observation 2
controls.help: Sets the x coordinate of observation 2. Changing the value changes predicted y for observation 2, residual 2, squared residual 2, the squared-residual vector, and total squared error.

controls.label: observed y of observation 2
controls.help: Sets the observed y coordinate of observation 2. Changing the value changes residual 2, squared residual 2, the squared-residual vector, and total squared error.

controls.label: slope m
controls.help: Sets the slope m of the candidate line. Changing the value changes predicted y for both observations, both residuals, both squared residuals, the squared-residual vector, and total squared error.

controls.label: intercept b
controls.help: Sets the intercept b of the candidate line. Changing the value shifts predicted y for both observations, changing both residuals, both squared residuals, the squared-residual vector, and total squared error.

explorations.title: Line through both points
explorations.instruction: Predict: will the total squared error reach zero when the line passes through both observations? Then apply the preset, which sets slope and intercept.
explorations.observe: Residual 1 and residual 2 become zero, squared residual 1 and squared residual 2 become zero, the squared-residual vector becomes [0, 0], and total squared error SSE becomes 0.
explorations.why: The preset line has predicted y equal to observed y at both x values, so each residual y_i - yhat_i is zero and each squared residual is zero. The total squared error is the sum of those zeros.

explorations.title: Steeper slope raises error
explorations.instruction: Predict: if slope increases while intercept and observations stay fixed, will total squared error rise or fall? Then apply the preset, which sets slope and intercept.
explorations.observe: Predicted y for observation 2 jumps above the observed value, so residual 2 and squared residual 2 shrink; predicted y for observation 1 drops further below the observed value, so residual 1 and squared residual 1 grow much more; total squared error SSE rises from 4.5 to 6.5.
explorations.why: Predicted y is intercept + slope times x. A larger slope lowers the prediction at the negative x of observation 1 and raises the prediction at the positive x of observation 2. Squaring makes the larger mismatch at observation 1 dominate, so total squared error increases.

tests.name: line through both points gives zero error
